sources.recourse_note: The 'recourse_keys' below are verbatim excerpts that the Recourse repository (read-only, commit 721e063) already holds in chunks/*.json and lists in judgment_doctrine_map.py, ndps_doctrine_map.py, cheque_bounce_doctrine_map.py or domestic_violence_doctrine_map.py as hand-verified. Their notes call them read verbatim against the judgment; nothing in them says a lawyer checked them. The cases were chosen by Recourse's own curation, not by this project's search.

rules.match: a key paragraph is found when 50% of its 8-word runs are in the passages that hold it (a passage holds it if it has 30% of the key's runs or half of its own runs are the key's)
rules.split: frozen only if unexposed and the whole group is unexposed; free groups split inside each area by SHA-256(seed|group), alternating frozen, dev
rules.exposed: a topic is exposed once search results for it have been seen; the first six topics were scored, rewritten and discussed before this file existed

questions.text: Can the police arrest me automatically just because a case under 498A has been registered against me?
questions.rewrite: Whether police may arrest an accused as a matter of course on registration of an FIR for an offence under Section 498A IPC, or must be satisfied that arrest is necessary under Section 41 CrPC (arrest without warrant).

questions.text: Must a police officer be satisfied that arrest is necessary under Section 41 CrPC before arresting for an offence punishable up to seven years, and what must the magistrate check at remand?
My neighbour filed a police case of cheating and forgery over a land dispute that is really a civil matter. Can criminal law be used for this?
questions.rewrite: Whether a dispute that is essentially civil in nature, concerning land or property, can be made the basis of a criminal complaint of cheating and forgery under the IPC, and when criminal proceedings may be quashed as an abuse of process.

questions.text: Can a civil dispute about ownership of property be given a criminal colour by alleging forgery of documents?
Both parties have settled a case of grievous hurt. Can the court accept the compromise or reduce the sentence even though the offence is non-compoundable?
questions.rewrite: Whether a court can permit compounding of, or reduce the sentence in view of a compromise between the parties for, the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means (Section 326 IPC), which is not compoundable under Section 320 CrPC.
questions.rewrite_v1: Whether a court can permit compounding of, or reduce the sentence in view of a compromise between the parties for, the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt, which is not compoundable under Section 320 CrPC.
questions.rewrite_note: The v1 hand rewrite called voluntarily causing grievous hurt (Section 325) 'not compoundable under Section 320'. The question text itself is unchanged (it only says 'grievous hurt' and 'non-compoundable'), so Q05's marks stand; versions C and F for Q05 were run on the old rewrite and need re-running and re-marking.

questions.text: Can the Supreme Court reduce the sentence on the basis of a compromise in an offence under Section 325 IPC that cannot be compounded under Section 320?

marks.note: these marks answer the old wording; kept as a record

questions.text: Can the Supreme Court reduce the sentence on the basis of a compromise in an offence under Section 326 IPC that cannot be compounded under Section 320?
questions.correction_reason: Q06 said Section 325. Section 325 IPC is compoundable with the court's permission under Section 320(2); the landmark (Nanda Gopalan) concerns Sections 324 and 326, which are not in Section 320. The old passages were found with a section search on 325, so they are not a fair pool for the corrected question: Q06v2 needs a new pool and new marks.

marks.note: needs a new pool (the old one came from a section search on 325) and new marks

questions.text: The cheque bounced and the accused says he never owed any money. Who has to prove the debt?
questions.rewrite: Burden of proof and statutory presumptions under the Negotiable Instruments Act where a cheque is dishonoured and the drawer denies any legally enforceable debt or liability; Sections 138, 118 and 139.

questions.text: Does the presumption under Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act cover the existence of a legally enforceable debt, and how can it be rebutted?
Police searched me for drugs but only vaguely said I could be searched in front of an officer. Is that enough?
questions.rewrite: Whether telling a person to be searched for narcotics that he may be searched before a Gazetted Officer or Magistrate, without clearly informing him of his right, satisfies the mandatory requirement of Section 50 of the NDPS Act.

questions.text: Is substantial compliance enough with the requirement under Section 50 of the NDPS Act to inform the accused of the right to be searched before a Gazetted Officer or Magistrate?
They found drugs and say I must prove I am innocent. Do I have to prove it?
questions.rewrite: Whether the burden of proof can be placed on the accused in a prosecution for possession of narcotic drugs under the NDPS Act: the presumption of culpable mental state under Section 35 and the standard of proof the accused must meet.

questions.text: Is the reverse burden under Sections 35 and 54 of the NDPS Act constitutional, and what must the prosecution establish first?
The police took my brother away and never gave him or us anything in writing to say why he was arrested. Is that allowed?
